evidence_levels.A: Analytical identity, exact solution, or limiting case
evidence_levels.B: Parity with the MATLAB or Octave reference implementation
evidence_levels.C: Comparison with an independent numerical tool or implementation
evidence_levels.D: Published benchmark, theory curve, or literature dataset
evidence_levels.R: Regression, invariant, or internal cross-backend check

records.claim: Core rotations, echo conversion, acquisition, and arb10 propagation reproduce the established MATLAB/Octave implementation.
records.basis: CSV fixtures generated from MATLAB R2025b or Octave 11.3, plus rotation-matrix invariants.
records.parameter_range: Compact offset grids and ideal/tuned/untuned/matched reference parameter sets stored in validation/fixtures.
records.metric: Elementwise numerical agreement
records.tolerance: Per-test numpy.testing tolerances, normally 1e-10 to 1e-7 absolute/relative.
references: MATLABSpinDynamics/Version_3/code
limitations: Fixtures sample representative grids; they are not an exhaustive proof over all parameter combinations.

records.component: CPMG, FID, imaging, and probe workflows
records.claim: Public ideal, tuned, untuned, and matched workflow assemblies preserve the reference signal and result conventions.
records.basis: MATLAB/Octave workflow fixtures, result-shape checks, and serial/parallel equality tests.
records.parameter_range: Representative finite/asymptotic echo trains, Q and mistuning sweeps, and compact imaging phantoms.
records.metric: Array agreement and workflow invariants
records.tolerance: Fixture-specific numerical tolerances; exact equality for deterministic serial/parallel paths.
references: MATLABSpinDynamics/Version_3/code
limitations: High-Q matched-probe coverage remains concentrated on compact fixtures.

records.component: Probe pulse responses and phase programs
records.claim: Rectangular tuned, untuned, and matched pulse responses and selected phase-program helpers match the MATLAB implementation.
records.basis: MATLAB/Octave waveform and catalog fixtures.
records.parameter_range: Bundled rectangular-pulse fixtures and selected SPA phase programs.
records.metric: Complex waveform and scalar metric agreement
records.tolerance: Per-fixture numerical tolerances, normally near floating-point precision.
references: MATLABSpinDynamics/Version_3/code/Pulse Shape
limitations: Arbitrary measured probe transfer functions are not covered by the historical fixtures.

records.component: Sequence IR, Pulseq interchange, and compiler
records.claim: Core Pulseq 1.4/1.5 events retain timing and metadata through import, compilation, plotting data, facade execution, and raster-aligned 1.5.0 round trips.
records.basis: Hand-audited Pulseq text fixtures, round-trip checks, exact timing assertions, moving-isochromat facade parity, and signature verification.
records.parameter_range: Core RF, arbitrary/trapezoid gradients, ADC, compressed shapes, offsets, and block timing.
records.metric: Exact metadata/timing invariants and numerical waveform equality
records.tolerance: Exact for discrete metadata; 1e-12 seconds or tighter for timing comparisons.
references: Pulseq specification 1.4.x and 1.5.0
limitations: No independent scanner/vendor execution comparison yet.
Optional extensions are retained but not executed.

records.claim: The deterministic moment backend follows the Stejskal-Tanner b-value and exp(-bD) attenuation, and free walkers converge toward that result.
records.basis: Closed-form Stejskal-Tanner equations and an independently sampled random-walker backend.
records.parameter_range: Rectangular lobes, unrestricted isotropic diffusion, zero-gradient/diffusion limits, and compact walker ensembles.
records.metric: b-value equality, log-signal slope, and walker confidence envelope
records.tolerance: Machine precision for moments; statistical tolerance set from finite walker count for particle simulations.
references: Stejskal-Tanner pulsed-gradient spin-echo theory
limitations: The analytical comparison assumes unrestricted isotropic diffusion and ideal rectangular gradients.

records.claim: Seeded particle motion has the expected diffusion statistics, boundary behavior, RF rotation, and static-gradient refocusing limits.
records.basis: Brownian mean-square displacement, deterministic zero-diffusion limits, and sequence refocusing invariants.
records.parameter_range: One to three spatial dimensions with reflecting/periodic boundaries on sampled domains.
records.metric: Moment statistics, signal limits, and deterministic seed equality
records.tolerance: Analytical or sampling-error tolerance chosen per test.
references: Brownian diffusion and spin-echo refocusing identities
limitations: Complex pore geometries have synthetic rather than experimental benchmarks.

records.claim: Plug and laminar pipe washout and flux-weighted transit polarization follow their analytical distributions and Monte Carlo estimates.
records.basis: Closed-form residence-time distributions and independent Monte Carlo sampling.
records.parameter_range: Ideal plug and fully developed laminar flow in a cylindrical sensitive region.
records.metric: Survival fraction, density normalization, mean transit time, and polarization
records.tolerance: Exact/near-machine precision for identities; finite-sample bounds for Monte Carlo checks.
references: Poiseuille flow and flux-weighted residence-time theory
limitations: No CFD or turbulent-flow comparison; velocity profiles are prescribed.

records.claim: Biot-Savart coil fields and selected magnet geometries reproduce analytical center-field, symmetry, scaling, finite-length, and far-field limits; the documented AlNiCo electropermanent rod also reproduces its published surface-field benchmark.
records.basis: Circular-loop center field, symmetry planes, current scaling, known Halbach field orientation, exact finite-cylinder axial fields, point-dipole limits, and a published AlNiCo-5 rod benchmark.
records.parameter_range: Loop coils, yoke-image checks, finite Halbach rods, NMR-MOUSE-scale grids, and finite cylindrical AlNiCo rods and bundles.
records.metric: Vector-field value, direction, symmetry, and scaling
records.tolerance: Geometry/discretization-specific tolerances declared in tests.
references: Biot-Savart circular-loop solution
Ideal Halbach dipole symmetry
Weinberg Medical Physics variable-field NMR AlNiCo rod measurements
limitations: Static field evaluation consumes a retained state supplied directly or by a programming model; quasistatic self-demagnetizing and neighbor coupling are handled by the separate coupled programmer rather than the field evaluator itself.

records.component: Electropermanent programming pulses and retained state
records.claim: The NumPy capacitor/H-bridge/series-RLC integrator reproduces the exact underdamped current solution and configuration-specific fits recover the archived 220/400/600-V peak-current examples; empirical remanence updates enforce their calibrated branch, polarity, range, uncertainty, and provenance.
records.basis: Exact underdamped series-RLC current, electrical energy balance, archived peak-current traces, and protocol invariants for the coarse published demagnetization envelope.
records.parameter_range: 10--50 us gates, 220--600 V capacitor commands, approximately 147--330 A measured peaks, passive recovery, and a 0--100 percent saturate-then-demagnetize command.
records.metric: Current waveform and peak, energy residual, temperature direction, retained remanence, branch, reversal point, and uncertainty
records.tolerance: 2e-8 relative for the analytical RLC waveform; 4 percent for configuration-specific archived peak-current fits; exact protocol guards and interpolation anchors.
references: Weinberg archive MRI/IGBT_board/experimental results.pdf
Weinberg archive NQR_proposal_2019 demagnetization figure
Series-RLC transient solution
limitations: Effective L/R/C values are inferred fits rather than independently measured parameters for every trace; the three-anchor remanence envelope is not raw hysteresis data and cannot predict arbitrary minor loops. The separate return-point model is currently illustrative rather than measured.

records.component: Electropermanent return-point memory and neighbor coupling
records.claim: Weighted play operators close nested reversal loops exactly and obey wiping-out, while finite-geometry two-element coupling has the expected symmetry and sign and the self-demagnetizing programming fixed point converges.
records.basis: Scalar play-operator return-point identities, finite-magnet dipole symmetry, and explicit fixed-point residual checks.
records.parameter_range: Illustrative six-operator AlNiCo model over plus/minus 400 kA/m, side-by-side finite rods, optional diagonal demagnetizing factors, and one programmed target per solve.
records.metric: Loop-closure error, retained remanence, coupling-matrix sign and symmetry, iteration count, and fixed-point residual
records.tolerance: Machine precision for exact nested-loop closure; geometry-specific symmetry tolerances and 1 uT retained-remanence convergence in regression tests.
references: Scalar play-operator hysteresis and return-point memory
Finite magnetic-dipole interaction symmetry
limitations: The bundled thresholds, weights, saturation remanence, and temperature coefficient are illustrative inferred values rather than a measured AlNiCo minor-loop fit; transient winding interaction is handled by a separate multi-channel model whose coupling matrices require measurement.

records.claim: The multi-winding integrator reduces to the isolated RLC driver at zero coupling, produces the Lenz-law neighbor-current sign for positive mutual inductance, closes the coupled electrical-energy balance, and propagates pulse-driven disturbance into every return-point state.
records.basis: Zero-coupling reduction, initial coupled-inductor derivative sign, capacitor plus coupled-inductor energy conservation with resistive loss, and synthetic threshold-crossing regressions.
records.parameter_range: Two closed recovery windings, dimensionless mutual coefficients through 0.15, 20--30 us gates, 50--100 V commands, winding leakage through 0.20, and state-dependent self inductance through 25 percent.
records.metric: Current and induced-voltage sign, waveform deviation from isolated drive, energy residual, internal field, retained-state change, and fixed-point residual
records.tolerance: 2e-12 waveform reduction tolerance, 0.02 percent relative energy residual, exact sign/threshold checks, and 2 uT retained-state convergence.
references: Coupled-inductor circuit equations and Lenz's law
Weinberg archive 20200525 IGBT update neighbor-effect observations
limitations: Inactive channels are modeled as closed through recovery resistors; open, actively clamped, and multiplexed topologies are not yet available. Mutual inductance and winding-field leakage are explicit inferred inputs because no measured array matrix is bundled.

records.component: Hybrid electropermanent array and operating-state synthesis
records.claim: The cached fixed-plus-programmable field basis exactly reproduces direct finite-magnet superposition, and bounded synthesis recovers representable targets while reducing the reference field-off residual and preserving a requested transport-gradient sign.
records.basis: Linearity of magnetostatic fields in retained remanence, direct-versus-cached finite-rod field comparison, exact synthetic bounded least squares, and full 18-sub-unit array regressions.
records.parameter_range: Two illustrative opposing 3-by-3 panels with 18 hybrid sub-units, 72 AlNiCo controls, retained-remanence limits of plus/minus 0.33 T, compact control-region samples, uniform imaging and field-off targets, and affine transport gradients.
records.metric: Vector-field equality, target residual, reference-to-field-off RMS reduction, retained-state bounds, saturation count, and fitted centerline gradient sign
records.tolerance: Floating-point equality for cached/direct superposition and representable synthetic targets; geometry-specific reduction and gradient-sign checks for the illustrative full array.
references: Magnetostatic superposition and linearity in magnetization
Weinberg project evidence for the 18-sub-unit, 72-control hierarchy and control-region intent
limitations: The exact historical rod dimensions, pitch, and within-sub-unit layout are inferred illustrative assumptions until CAD or measured field bases are available.

Transport synthesis targets an affine projected static field; particle dynamics are tracked by a separate validation record, while programming schedules and closed-loop control are not yet included. Nonlinear imaging is also tracked separately.

records.claim: Retained-state fields generate the expected receiver-demodulated phase matrix, and nonnegative regularized inversion reproducibly reconstructs a noisy two-tissue phantom while localizing its off-center target.
records.basis: Direct cached-field evaluation, the analytical phase relation gamma times encoding duration times field offset, seeded complex-noise regression, and a known synthetic proton-density/T1/T2 phantom.
records.parameter_range: Illustrative 18-sub-unit/72-control array, 10-by-10 through 16-by-16 Cartesian tissue phantoms over 40 mm, 160 through 384 retained-state acquisitions, 250--300 us phase encoding, and 35 dB RMS acquisition SNR.
records.metric: Field and phase equality, matrix magnitude, inverse-system condition number, image NRMSE, convergence, repeatability, and target-centroid error
records.tolerance: Floating-point field/phase identities; below 3 percent NRMSE and condition number below 10 for the compact seeded regression.
references: General spatial encoding matrix s_k = sum_j rho_j exp(-i phi_kj)
Known synthetic tissue phantom generated by the package
limitations: Tissue relaxation constants, encoding states, array geometry, and noise are illustrative rather than measured platform data.

The workflow models one static phase-encoding interval per retained state and a real nonnegative spin-echo image; RF excitation, EPM programming time, eddy-current transients, off-resonance relaxation during readout, and multi-coil sensitivity encoding are not yet coupled.
Synthetic reconstruction validates the implemented inverse but is not an independent experimental or scanner benchmark.

records.component: Susceptibility-aware EPM particle MR sequence comparison
records.claim: A selected retained EPM state supplies the background B0 map; field-dependent equivalent-sphere particle moments generate subvoxel dipole perturbations while magnetic-core samples exclude water signal; paired finite-pulse spin echo, Cartesian GRE, GRE phase-gradient mapping, and center-out radial short-TE acquisitions propagate tissue relaxation and diffusing water; and reference-supported contrast yields image-derived susceptibility foci and centroids without reading particle truth.
records.basis: Uniformly magnetized sphere interior and exterior dipole identities, direct EPM field-basis evaluation, explicit finite-pulse spin echo and GRE propagation, paired complex phase derivatives, center-out non-Cartesian encoding, paired seeded random-walker diffusion, and synthetic contrast-localization fixtures.
records.parameter_range: Two-dimensional uniform Cartesian tissue maps; one through nine subvoxel samples per axis; non-negative water diffusion; one or more walkers per voxel; linear or Langevin particle magnetization; finite excitation, refocusing, phase-encoding, Cartesian-readout, and radial-readout durations; optional per-acquisition relative complex noise.
records.metric: Dipole-field sign and symmetry, nonzero particle delta B0, selected EPM background field, spatial subvoxel propagation, center-k-space time, resolved contrast foci, centroid error, symmetric nearest-focus error, controller consumption of the reconstructed outside-target centroid, and seeded repeatability.
records.tolerance: Floating-point dipole symmetry identities; exact configuration and seeded-output identities; positive physical contrast in the compact regression; centroid error is reported because blooming depends strongly on size, field, sequence, and resolution.
references: Mani et al., Magnetic Resonance in Medicine 55 (2006), 126-135, DOI 10.1002/mrm.20739
Zhao et al., NMR in Biomedicine 24 (2011), 464-472, DOI 10.1002/nbm.1608
Gharagouzloo et al., Magnetic Resonance in Medicine 74 (2015), 431-441, DOI 10.1002/mrm.25426
limitations: The equivalent-sphere field does not yet model rod orientation, nonspherical demagnetization, particle-particle magnetic interaction, aggregation-dependent magnetization, or microscopic water exchange.

The acquisition engines model a two-dimensional slice with ideal rectangular RF drive, scalar B1 maps, Cartesian or ideal center-out gradients, and a mesoscopic subvoxel/random-walker approximation; they are not scanner-validated Bloch-Torrey calculations.

The radial short-TE path does not infer concentration-dependent T1 relaxivity or steady-state saturation, and optional SNR is relative per acquisition rather than bandwidth- and scan-time-matched absolute noise.

Target contrast fraction is not particle occupancy or particle count. Static spin echo suppresses susceptibility sensitivity, while finite-bandwidth, phase-gradient, radial-undersampling, and readout effects cause blooming or artifact foci and can shift the recovered centroid.
The example uses an illustrative 100 um effective magnetic core and disables receiver noise by default to isolate sequence physics; it is not an injectable-particle detectability claim.

records.claim: The transport workflow recovers the analytical linear superparamagnetic force and Stokes--Einstein limits, smoothly caps magnetization with a Langevin law, differentiates affine fields correctly, and reproducibly integrates seeded flow/diffusion trajectories with target capture.
records.basis: Closed-form force, Stokes drag, Stokes--Einstein diffusion, and affine-field gradient identities plus seeded synthetic trajectory regressions coupled to the known tissue phantom.
records.parameter_range: Two-dimensional sampled vector fields; positive SI particle radii, viscosity, temperature, and saturation magnetization; non-negative susceptibility; linear and Langevin magnetization; rectangular reflect, periodic, and clip boundaries; constant, array, or callable background velocities.
records.metric: Force vector, magnetization limit, diffusion coefficient, grad(|B|^2), trajectory repeatability, cumulative capture monotonicity, peak force, and capture fraction
records.tolerance: Floating-point analytical identities; seeded trajectory equality; qualitative positive capture in the compact regression.
references: Linear superparamagnetic force F = V chi grad(|B|^2)/(2 mu0)
Langevin magnetization, Stokes drag, and Stokes--Einstein diffusion
limitations: The integrated example uses an illustrative 30 um hydrodynamic magnetic aggregate and inferred array geometry, not a calibrated nanoparticle formulation or clinical dose.

The first transport model is dilute and overdamped; it omits particle-particle interactions, aggregation kinetics, adhesion and release kinetics, branching vasculature, porous tissue permeability, hydrodynamic wall corrections, and feedback on field or flow.
Target capture is irreversible on entry to a circle. The alternating controller is tracked by a separate validation record.

records.claim: The controller executes contiguous image-program-transport-verification intervals, supports the calibrated direct-signal baseline and selectable susceptibility-aware spin echo, GRE, GRE phase-gradient, or radial short-TE acquisition, re-aims each affine transport objective from the reconstructed outside-target centroid, and stops reproducibly from verification imaging rather than simulator truth.
records.basis: Cloud-in-cell conservation identities, exact noiseless image-state recovery cases, state-machine interval identities, direct estimated-centroid direction geometry, seeded noisy nonlinear reconstructions and Brownian paths, retained-state total variation, and persistent-capture regressions.
records.parameter_range: One through four cycles in compact regressions and examples; 5-by-5 estimator identity grids and 10-by-10 through 20-by-20 EPM encoding/force grids; 3 through 80 illustrative magnetic aggregates; configurable target, particle, and verification imaging noise/regularization, signal per particle, support threshold, boundary-capture partial-volume correction, timing windows, and capture goals in (0, 1].
records.metric: Deposited signal and first moment, recovered count and representative positions, target and particle centroids, occupancy, centroid/occupancy error against hidden truth, mode order and contiguity, requested direction, remanence variation, force, stopping reason, and seeded repeatability
records.tolerance: Floating-point deposition, centroid, interval, and direction identities; exact noiseless count/occupancy fixtures; exact seeded output equality; image-derived configured stopping semantics; noisy estimator error is reported rather than hidden by a fixed acceptance claim.
references: Cloud-in-cell concentration imaging and image-moment identities
Feedback state-machine and centroid steering identities
Package nonlinear EPM imaging and magnetophoretic transport validation records
limitations: The direct-signal baseline uses a supplied signal per aggregate and is not a physical MR contrast mechanism. The susceptibility options are physical but uncalibrated and their target contrast fraction is not a particle count or occupancy measurement.

Recovered positions are representative image-resolved distribution samples or susceptibility foci, not identity-preserving tracks. The direct-channel boundary-capture partial-volume correction follows from the simulated first-entry capture rule and grid geometry; it requires experimental validation and does not apply to blooming physical contrast.

Summed retained-remanence variation is a programming-effort metric, not pulse count, switching energy, temperature, or driver stress. A calibrated 72-channel programming schedule is required for those quantities.
The controller inherits the illustrative array, aggregate, dilute transport, irreversible circular capture, and missing vascular/tissue physics of the component models.

records.claim: The workflow executes the published polarize-delay-antialigned-gradient timing, recovers spherical Stokes and Tirado finite-cylinder diffusion limits, reproducibly couples rigid-body and magnetic-moment orientation to translation, distinguishes contraction from rapidly relaxing-moment expansion, and makes coil, EPM-only, and hybrid switching burdens explicit.
records.basis: Closed-form Stokes and rotational Einstein limits, the two-dimensional polar-orientation correlation exp(-D_r*t), published Tirado finite-cylinder diffusion expressions, the Nacev 2015 pulse order and timing, seeded stochastic trajectory regression, and exact architecture pulse-count identities.
records.parameter_range: Two-dimensional dilute particles represented as spheres or rods with rod aspect ratio at least 2; rigid or finite internal moment relaxation; four-direction inverse-power source model; configurable polarizer, gradient, geometry, flow, Brownian motion, reflecting bounds, timing, EPM parallelism, and optional calibrated pulse energies.
records.metric: Translational and rotational drag/diffusion, deterministic and Brownian-limited effective orientation-memory time, repulsive gradient fraction, RMS-radius concentration gain, target retention and escape, seeded repeatability, state/channel pulse count, timing margin, waveform fidelity, and average power when energy inputs are supplied
records.tolerance: Floating-point analytical drag/diffusion and two-dimensional polar-correlation identities; exact seeded trajectory equality; qualitative contraction for the compact rigid long-rod case and expansion for its 100 ns internal-relaxation control; exact integer hardware counts and a Brownian-dominated infeasibility regression.
references: Nacev et al., Nano Letters 15 (2015), 359-364, DOI 10.1021/nl503654t
Tirado, Martinez, and Garcia de la Torre, Journal of Chemical Physics 81 (1984), 2047-2052, DOI 10.1063/1.447827
limitations: The analytical inverse-power gradient sources are inferred and are not reconstructed from measured coil or EPM field maps; the implementation therefore validates mechanism and trends, not the published concentration rate.

The model is two-dimensional, dilute, overdamped, and noninteracting; it omits aggregation, rod flexibility, walls beyond rectangular reflection, tissue adhesion, vascular branching, collisions, and fluid-structure coupling.
The finite internal-relaxation option is a phenomenological moment-angle relaxation, not a microscopic Neel/domain model. Tirado fitted end corrections are extrapolated above aspect ratio 30.

EPM-only waveform fidelity defaults to infeasible because retained-state programming transients are not calibrated as therapeutic polarize/gradient pulses. Hybrid EPM bias/shaping does not yet synthesize a specific 72-element state or include its static force perturbation.
Energy and average power remain unavailable unless architecture-specific coil and EPM pulse energies are supplied.

records.claim: PEEC inductance/resistance trends agree with analytical kernels and selected independent QOIL, FastHenry, and FasterCap comparisons.
records.basis: Partial-element analytical kernels, bundled QOIL regression values, and optional live external-solver comparisons.
records.parameter_range: Round-wire loops and compact solenoids represented by the bundled test geometries.
records.metric: Inductance, resistance, capacitance, and impedance deviation
records.tolerance: Tool- and discretization-specific thresholds declared in PEEC tests.
references: QOIL
FastHenry
FasterCap
limitations: Live external-tool tests are optional and not run in ordinary CI.
Validation is sparse for shields, complex windings, and high-frequency radiation.

records.component: Coupled receiver networks, resonant cancellation, active LNAs, and passive interconnects
records.claim: Loaded sensitivity, passive noise covariance, shared-capacitor cancellation, separated active-LNA noise, and reciprocal two-port interconnects reduce to analytical multiport and Friis limits while mutual resistance remains after mutual reactance is cancelled.
records.basis: Exact two-loop mesh equations, fluctuation-dissipation noise covariance, active one-port voltage/current/cross-noise identities, reciprocal ABCD transformations, the matched-line Friis limit, single-frequency solver agreement, and passive-matrix invariants.
records.parameter_range: Reciprocal passive terminal-impedance matrices with two or more ports; independent per-channel reciprocal passive two-ports; analytical two-loop and matched-line cases near 1-2 MHz; and a compact two-solenoid PEEC example.
records.metric: Residual mutual reactance, induced-current isolation, transformed coil-port load, voltage transfer, separated output-noise covariance, insertion loss/noise figure, optimal array SNR, and noise correlation
records.tolerance: Machine-precision analytical identities and per-test numerical tolerances; the PEEC geometry, sample-loss values, interconnect, and LNA values are illustrative rather than experimentally calibrated.
references: Hoult and Richards, Journal of Magnetic Resonance 24 (1976), 71-85, DOI 10.1016/0022-2364(76)90233-X
Roemer et al., Magnetic Resonance in Medicine 16 (1990), 192-225, DOI 10.1002/mrm.1910160203
Wang et al., Magnetic Resonance in Medicine 89 (2023), 859-871, DOI 10.1002/mrm.29489
Sun et al., Magnetic Resonance in Medicine 90 (2023), 2198-2210, DOI 10.1002/mrm.29755
limitations: The passive cancellation and interconnect sweeps remain uniform-temperature terminal models.
Passive front ends are independent per-channel reciprocal two-ports; coupled transmission lines and measured S-parameter import are pending.

The active model separates diagonal LNA R-X||C loading, voltage/current/cross noise, gain, and downstream noise, but standard noise-parameter conversion, cross-channel amplifier noise, stability, compression, and direct Experiment integration remain pending.
The sample-loss matrices, conductor geometry, cable, and LNA values are illustrative, with no scanner or bench comparison yet.

Cancellation removes mutual reactance at one frequency but not mutual resistance or sensitivity to loading and tolerances; transformed low input impedance can improve isolation without providing a noise match.

records.claim: Lumped, one-dimensional, axisymmetric, perfused, and advective thermal models reproduce closed-form limits; coupled electromagnets recover exact RL and electrothermal fixed points, and selected conduction cases are cross-checked with FEMM.
records.basis: RC and RL exponential responses, electrothermal fixed points, slab/cylinder/sphere source solutions, conservation laws, advection-diffusion solutions, and FEMM scripts.
records.parameter_range: Constant-property thermal materials, temperature-dependent conductor resistance, standard boundary conditions, and selected coupled coil/sample/electromagnet cases.
records.metric: Temperature, current, B0, energy balance, steady-state rise, and transient time constant
records.tolerance: Analytical solver/discretization tolerances declared per test and FEMM validation script.
references: FEMM
Classical heat-equation and Pennes limits
limitations: No general full-3D or CFD thermal validation.
Electromagnet validation is analytical and does not cover nonlinear ferromagnetic cores or measured supply/sensor dynamics.

records.claim: Spin-1 and spin-3/2 transition conventions, powder weights, selective pulses, and SORC/SLSE limits reproduce analytical and published theory results.
records.basis: Angular-momentum identities, closed-form quadrupole transitions, Konnai SORC theory, and the published Glickstein melamine enhancement example.
records.parameter_range: Spin 1 and 3/2 core cases, axial/asymmetric EFGs, single-crystal and powder grids, and weak-B0 limits.
records.metric: Frequency, population transfer, normalized powder signal, and operator identities
records.tolerance: Analytical numerical tolerances declared per test; published-example agreement at reported precision.
references: Konnai SORC powder theory
Glickstein spin-1 polarization enhancement example
limitations: Experimental waveform and absolute-signal comparisons remain limited.
Higher-spin validation is primarily analytical rather than experimental.

records.claim: Zeeman resonance, lineshape, hyperfine splitting, relaxation, and Hahn-echo behavior reproduce analytical spin-1/2 limits.
records.basis: Bohr-magneton resonance, Hermiticity/scaling identities, exact isotropic hyperfine doublets, and echo-refocusing theory.
records.parameter_range: Single-electron spin-1/2 systems with scalar/anisotropic g, simple hyperfine systems, static disorder, and phenomenological T1/T2.
records.metric: Resonance field/frequency, splitting, normalization, decay, and echo timing
records.tolerance: Analytical numerical tolerances declared per test.
references: Standard spin-1/2 ESR resonance and hyperfine formulas
limitations: No broad experimental spectral library comparison.
Multi-electron and general anisotropic hyperfine systems remain incomplete.

records.claim: Dense spin operators, scalar-coupling Hamiltonians, and selected low-field editing models satisfy exact operator and spectral limits.
records.basis: Commutators, Hermiticity, trace conservation, exact two-spin energy levels, and synthetic editing limits.
records.parameter_range: Small dense spin-1/2 systems and the implemented J-editing/TANGO/SLIC models.
records.metric: Operator identities, eigenvalues, populations, and filter response
records.tolerance: Near floating-point precision for algebraic identities.
references: Exact spin-1/2 angular-momentum and scalar-coupling solutions
limitations: Paper-level fixtures and relaxation-aware general pulse-sequence comparisons are still sparse.

records.component: Singlet, triplet, and parahydrogen state primitives
records.claim: Embedded spin-pair singlet/triplet projectors, swap symmetry, singlet-order observables, and para/ortho hydrogen mixtures satisfy exact spin-1/2 algebra and physical density-matrix limits.
records.basis: Exact singlet/triplet projector identities, pair-permutation eigenvalues, trace and positivity constraints, and the para-H2 statistical-mixture identity rho=I/4+(f_p-1/4)Q_S.
records.parameter_range: Spin-1/2 pairs embedded in two- and three-spin systems; para fractions from 0 to 1.
records.metric: Hermiticity, idempotence, orthogonality, completeness, trace, eigenvalues, population, and singlet-order amplitude
records.tolerance: Floating-point algebraic tolerance of 1e-10 or tighter.
references: Carravetta and Levitt, J. Am. Chem. Soc. 126 (2004) 6228-6229, doi:10.1021/ja0490931
DeVience, Walsworth, and Rosen, arXiv:1307.0832
limitations: This record validates state algebra and ideal SLIC limits; workflow-level LLS and PHIP invariants are tracked separately.

records.component: Long-lived singlet and hydrogenative PHIP reference workflows
records.claim: SLIC preparation/storage/readout obeys its analytical matching and exponential T_S limits, while hydrogenative product order is physical and linear in para excess and pairwise-addition fraction.
records.basis: Exact dense two-spin propagation, trace and positivity checks, analytical singlet-mode exponential decay, product-state normalization, and linear PHIP source-order scaling.
records.parameter_range: Nearly equivalent two-proton SLIC pair; physical and deviation storage densities; two- and three-spin product mappings; para fractions from 0.25 to 1; pairwise fractions from 0 to 1; high-field PASADENA and explicit piecewise ALTADENA trajectories.
records.metric: Prepared singlet amplitude, normalized readout decay, trace, minimum density eigenvalue, PHIP FID amplitude, and linear scaling residual
records.tolerance: Floating-point invariant tolerance of 1e-10; ideal SLIC preparation amplitude within 0.002 of unity.
references: DeVience, Walsworth, and Rosen, arXiv:1307.0832
Cavallari et al., Frontiers in Oncology 11, 617307 (2021), doi:10.3389/fonc.2021.617307
limitations: T_S is a measured phenomenological input rather than a microscopic correlated-relaxation prediction.
Pairwise hydrogenation yield, catalyst chemistry, reaction-time distributions, and scrambling are external inputs or not yet modeled.
PASADENA and ALTADENA currently have algebraic and regression validation only; published spectral fixtures and PH-INEPT transfer remain to be added.

records.claim: Relaxation propagators preserve required invariants and limiting behavior; measured weak-field 35Cl SLSE relaxation is reproduced; the non-diagonal zero-field Redfield model reproduces published transition-resolved 209Bi FVA rate shapes; and RDX NMR/NQR observations recover the published activated barrier and cross-relaxation assignments.
records.basis: Trace/Hermiticity preservation, equilibrium limits, Chen et al. Table 1 measurements, 24 experimental plus published FA/FVA rates from Goesweiner et al. Table 1, Smith et al. RDX Figures 2 and 8, and a read-only audit of 89 NQRDatabase relaxation records.
records.parameter_range: Implemented Bloch, Liouville, BPP/Redfield, wall, and rotating-frame models; NaClO3 powder from 0 to 41 G; three 209Bi aryl compounds at 77 and 310 K with four transitions each; RDX 14N NQR from 266 to 340 K and 1H cross-relaxation minima from 0 to 540 kHz.
records.metric: Invariant diagnostics, experimental RMS rate residual, coupled/diagonal lowest-transition ratio, mean relative FVA rate-shape deviation, Arrhenius activation energy, and cross-relaxation resonance position
records.tolerance: NaClO3 RMS residual <= 10 s^-1 and nonzero-field T2 within 15%; 209Bi mean relative deviation from published FVA rate shapes < 10% after one amplitude scale per sample/temperature group; RDX activation energy within 4 kJ/mol of 92 kJ/mol and resonance centers within 10 kHz.
references: Bloch exponential relaxation
BPP and Redfield limiting formulas
Goesweiner et al., Molecular Physics 118, e1743888 (2020), doi:10.1080/00268976.2020.1743888
limitations: The NaClO3 field-independent floor and absolute cross-relaxation strength are fitted nuisance parameters.

The 209Bi validation fits one amplitude normalization per material/temperature group and is uneven for tris(4-fluorophenyl)bismuth at 77 K, where the published single-mode FVA model is also inaccurate.
RDX values are figure-digitized; differing sample preparations preclude a joint absolute-amplitude fit, and the full heteronuclear dispersion model is not yet implemented.
NQRDatabase has no immediately fit-eligible microscopic relaxation series and contains a factor-1000 sodium-nitrite source conflict.

records.component: ENDOR-QDyne coherent basis mapping and linewidth
records.claim: The resolved-spin ENDOR-QDyne model reproduces the ideal coherent-basis-mapping signal, phase-cycled carrier, weak-measurement back-action map, initialization-infidelity linewidth, and proof-of-principle timing reported by Meinel et al.
records.basis: Main-text Eqs. 1-3, Supplementary Eqs. 14 and 23, the reported operation timings, and direct deterministic regressions against the corresponding closed-form expressions.
records.parameter_range: Spin-one-half target; finite signed longitudinal Azz coupling in Hz; configurable RF reference, free-precession and sensing intervals, RF phase cycling, residual sensing phase, clock errors, sensor T2*, intrinsic nuclear decay, initialization fidelity, optional optical counts, and exact or disabled weak-measurement back-action; paper preset at Azz=6 kHz and 105.5 us repetition.
records.metric: Samplewise Iz and Sz expectation values, RF operation and total cycle time, baseband carrier and FFT peak, exact and leading initialization decay rates, and discrete back-action recurrence.
records.tolerance: Floating-point agreement for analytical identities; less than one Fourier bin for the simulated carrier; within 2 Hz of the reported 2.368 kHz phase-cycle target; the approximately 1 kHz Eq. 3 numerical estimate is reproduced as 1.012 kHz using the paper's 2*pi*Azz*Sz*Iz Hamiltonian and spectroscopic-Hz convention.
references: J. Meinel et al., Communications Physics 6 (2023) 302, doi:10.1038/s42005-023-01419-2
Supplementary Information for High-resolution nanoscale NMR for arbitrary magnetic fields, doi:10.21203/rs.3.rs-2826442/v1
limitations: The comparison uses the authors' published equations, sequence timings, and reported carrier/linewidth targets rather than a refit of deposited raw photon-count traces.

The source's nearby statement Azz*tau=0.63 rad omits the 2*pi conversion implied by its Hamiltonian and approximately 1 kHz estimate; the implementation explicitly treats Azz as a cyclic frequency in Hz.

RF basis mapping is ideal apart from an explicit residual sensing phase; off-resonant finite-pulse unitary errors, charge-state switching, excited-state hyperfine changes, and a microscopic optical reset channel are not propagated.
The model covers one resolved spin-one-half target and an effective optical readout, not a many-spin ENDOR ensemble or a calibrated high-field instrument.

records.component: Defect-spin nanoscale spectroscopy, MRI, and package integration
records.claim: Implemented defect, bath, control, optical, statistical, exact-cluster, motion, imaging, high-resolution, and facade layers satisfy their documented analytical identities and deterministic/seeded regression contracts.
records.basis: Spin-Hamiltonian eigenvalue and rotational-covariance identities; inverse-cube dipolar and layer-depth laws; sequence/filter integrals; polarization, Lorentzian normalization, Brownian MSD/drift/confinement and propagator-tail references, optical-count preparation/transfer, Qdyne visibility/alias/bin, memory-envelope, chemical-shift/J, and DNP limits; plus facade/direct delegation, config/archive round trips, Bayesian binding, and complexity gates.
records.parameter_range: Built-in diamond NV-minus and configurable 4H-SiC PL6 presets; supported isotope presets; uniform/voxel baths; small dense resolved clusters; seeded three-dimensional trajectories; scanning/array forward models; effective optical/SPAD models; coherent clocked tones; analytic planar statistical spectra; compact Qdyne facade experiments.
records.metric: Eigenvalues, tensor scaling/covariance, PSD integral and peak position, coherence, moments, photon-count statistics, reconstruction error, recovered beat/bin spacing, envelope decomposition, multiplet positions, polarization limits, facade result/config identity, planner feasibility, work units, memory, and loose wall time.
records.tolerance: Floating-point, seeded-statistical, reconstruction, and deliberately loose performance tolerances declared in tests.
references: C. L. Degen, F. Reinhard, and P. Cappellaro, Reviews of Modern Physics 89 (2017) 035002, doi:10.1103/RevModPhys.89.035002
S. Schmitt et al., Science 356 (2017) 832-837, doi:10.1126/science.aam5532
J. M. Boss et al., Science 356 (2017) 837-840, doi:10.1126/science.aam7009
limitations: The current evidence is analytical and synthetic regression evidence; it does not compare predictions with a calibrated NV, SiC, optical, or scanning experiment.

Defect and detector parameters are configurable phenomenology rather than ab initio or device-specific calibration, and the Phase-8 facade covers planar statistical spectra and coherent Qdyne rather than every expert nano-MR backend.

The Qdyne facade signal is a coherent classical tone; it does not make a statistically polarized nanoscale bath phase coherent. The Gaussian return-propagator tail is an analytic reference, not an end-to-end convergence validation of trajectory-derived dipolar correlations. Exact clusters remain small dense systems, and coherent chemical-shift/J and DNP models are effective first-order descriptions.

records.claim: Facade archives identify experiment inputs, implementation, numerical environment, randomness, and result content and can verify an exact rerun while remaining backward-compatible with version-1 archives.
records.basis: Canonical fingerprint invariance/change tests, archive integrity checks, seeded/unseeded classification, exact rerun comparison, CLI verification, and legacy archive loading.

records.component: Bayesian experiment design and adaptive acquisition
records.claim: Bayesian updates, goal utilities, planner-validated adapters, batched PGSE parity, surrogate validation, staged/adaptive scoring, paired end-to-end adapter benchmarks, recoverable live batches, discrete-target nuisance marginalization, and robustness diagnostics follow their stated numerical and decision-theory contracts.
records.basis: Direct Bayes-rule and dense mutual-information calculations, prior-predictive coverage, deterministic replay, facade binding tests, paired common-truth/common-noise adaptive-versus-fixed trials for every Phase 2 adapter, exact prediction-table identity checks, batched-vs-facade PGSE parity, atomic checkpoint replacement, pending-call recovery, complete-outcome validation, rejection exclusion, explicit latency accounting, exact polynomial recovery, held-out surrogate errors, linear-Gaussian screening limits, nuisance-only target-information cancellation, discrepancy variance addition, model dispatch, and recommendation sensitivity cases.
records.parameter_range: Scalar/vector real and complex Gaussian observations; finite Cartesian grids and weighted particles; finite candidate spaces; CPMG-IR, deterministic PGSE, NQR FID, ESR Hahn, and coherent Qdyne adapters; polynomial response surfaces; discrete target/model labels.
records.metric: Posterior probability, mutual information, expected variance reduction, credible coverage, ranking and replay identity, planner feasibility, batch parity, atomic recovery identity, accepted/rejected update count, latency budget status, surrogate RMSE/correlation, Monte Carlo sample allocation, mixture dispatch, sensitivity agreement, physical seconds, and measured planning wall time.
records.tolerance: Floating-point or Monte Carlo tolerances declared in tests; prior-predictive coverage is required not to under-cover its nominal discrete interval in the fixed-seed reference.
references: T. Rainforth et al., Statistical Science 39 (2024) 100-114, doi:10.1214/23-STS915
C. A. Waudby et al., Journal of Magnetic Resonance 326 (2021) 106937, doi:10.1016/j.jmr.2021.106937
limitations: The evidence validates numerical/statistical contracts and synthetic examples, not time savings on a physical instrument.

The paired adapter benchmarks draw truth from the same finite exact simulator table used for inference, so they do not test model mismatch, hardware artifacts, or time savings on a physical instrument.

The live adapter is synchronous orchestration with a synthetic instrument example; it is not a vendor driver, safety controller, authenticated transport, distributed scheduler, or physical-instrument validation.

Continuous-target EIG, continuous design optimization, particle rejuvenation, and non-myopic batch design are not yet implemented; prediction batching remains workflow-specific, and surrogate speedups are machine- and feature-dependent and require held-out validation.

records.component: Multi-frequency Bloch-Siegert phase and low-frequency RWA limits
records.claim: Exact lab-frame paired-offset propagation reproduces the Mandal-2014 Bloch-Siegert phase slope and fitted 90-degree pulse length, while the second-order common phase isolates the counter-rotating contribution omitted by the RWA.
records.basis: Mandal et al. Eq. 17 and Fig. 15 operating point, analytical second-order co/counter-rotating decomposition, and an independently integrated real lab-frame Bloch equation.
records.parameter_range: f0=1.48 MHz, paired offsets +/-25 kHz, T90=102 us, TBS=40-400 us for the published reproduction; 60 kHz-1.48 MHz for counter-rotating inversion identities.
records.metric: Paired phase endpoint, inferred T90, RWA slope agreement, and B0 inversion error
records.tolerance: Published endpoint within 1 degree, inferred T90 within 2 us, exact/RWA phase within 2.5%, and analytical B0 inversion at floating-point precision.
references: S. Mandal et al., Journal of Magnetic Resonance 242 (2014) 113-125, doi:10.1016/j.jmr.2014.02.019
limitations: The published comparison uses the reported equation, fit, and plotted endpoint rather than digitized raw experimental points; second-order B0 inversion requires weak drive, paired offsets away from poles, and common phase above the noise floor.
